newsitem.title: UK: Few bravehearts left in Bradys ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Few bravehearts left in Bradys ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Trading in emerging debt largely ground to a halt on Friday morning, with investors unwilling to push their luck any more ahead of next week's possible hike in U.S. interest rates.
"There's nothing moving at all...I don't think there's much more action to be seen now. People will have already placed their bets," a European bank trader said.
Traders said the market has probably already priced in a 25 basis point rise in the Fed funds rate at next Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

There was a brief flurry of selling in Russian debt pushing down Vneshekonombank dollar paper to 69-1/8 cents in the dollar at one stage, before climbing back to around New York closing levels of just under 70 cents.
There remain plenty of bulls in the market for Russia, at least until its Eurobond issue, probably in November, and a credit rating.

"Our favourite remains Russia," ANZ analyst Jerome Booth said. He cited an expected credit rating by October 10, the proposed Eurobond, and near completion of the agreement with commercial creditors to reschedule old Soviet debt.
The market also has support from President Boris Yeltsin's decree to hand over power to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin when he undergoes heart surgery.
Booth said he expected any Fed tightening to be more modest than some expect, which could point to a rally in U.S. Treasuries, with Bradys, already around record highs, following suit.
